parcel_gate_verdict is a periodically-refreshed UPSERT snapshot (publish-gate-sched.mjs), not a live view of parcel_record_cell. A writer job's --apply does not itself refresh this table. Before trusting a stored parcel_gate_verdict row as current, check its evaluated_at against your own write's timestamp, or read the live verdict directly via gate-rail-cli.mjs (expensive: ~17-75s per (county,rail) call under today's store load, so scope any live re-check to the specific rails you touched, never a blind full sweep).

A local product-repo clone can be silently a month-plus stale even when it looks like a normal checkout (P:/hauska-engine: local HEAD 2026-08-12, origin/main 2026-09-15). Always git fetch + compare against origin/main before trusting a cross-repo file read for a count/diff that will be quoted in a close -- this lane's own first count (16/23) was wrong until checked against origin/main (13/30, matching the dispatch).

Applying a rail writer for a real subset of a county's in-city population (not the whole county) moves that rail's gate verdict from EXCLUDED (zero coverage, invisible to grading, A-153's own 'three states wearing one word' finding) to REFUSE (real, partial, honestly-failing coverage) -- never to PASS, and never back to EXCLUDED. A partial-coverage apply is real, measurable, additive progress that will not show as an aggregate pass-count improvement in a per-county rail-verdict summary until full coverage lands; do not read 'no pass-count change' as 'no effect' without checking the individual rail's own verdict kind.

Why does get_smart_site's bake not refresh promptly after a parcel_record_cell write that changes a rail's real, gate-visible state? Fired on two independent writer jobs now (P-200's setback group, this lane's envelope group), both times with the bake's own runId/bakedAt provably predating the write. P-200's own OPEN item asked whether hauska-engine's services/retrieval-api or a related repo owns the trigger/cadence for this; still unanswered as of this close.
